C-STATS-DASH-PUSH.Name: Gateway pushes its funnel events to the owner's own analytics dashboard (dash.xronocode.com) — no Cloudflare read credentials anywhere
C-STATS-DASH-PUSH.Summary: The counting gateway (M-071) counts update checks and update clicks into Workers Analytics Engine, whose only read path is a Cloudflare account token — the owner rejected that credential shape twice (2026-11-02 "only a Workers token"; 2026-11-03 "the dashboard already collects everything, why another key"). The owner's own analytics dashboard (dash.xronocode.com, the avenex-outreach analytics-dashboard product) already collects events from all his sites through its server-to-server intake POST /api/v1/collect with a per-site ingest key — the same mechanism vektor, palabras and avenex use. This change makes the gateway a sender like any other site: on every counted event, alongside the existing best-effort Analytics Engine write, the worker fires one best-effort POST to the dashboard's collect endpoint with event name mark.update_check (props: os, from) or mark.update_pkg (props: platform, version), session "gateway", no identifiers beyond those aggregate dimensions. The only new credential is DASH_COLLECT_KEY — a dashboard-issued site ingest key the owner creates in his own dashboard UI (visible flow he already knows), stored as a Worker secret; no Cloudflare API token is created, read or needed, and the C-STATS-READOUT STATS_API_TOKEN saga is retired (the garbage secret and the dead mark-stats-reader token get deleted). Counting responses never change: the push rides ctx.waitUntil, failures are swallowed, and an absent secret disables the push entirely (pure no-op).

Problem.Description: (1) The readout of the update-funnel counters requires reading Workers Analytics Engine, whose binding is write-only — the only read path is the SQL REST API with an account-analytics bearer token. That token could not be provisioned by automation (Cloudflare shows the value exactly once; the dashboard-assisted attempt left an unusable secret) and the owner explicitly rejected the credential shape: the numbers should flow into his existing central analytics (owner, 2026-11-03, translated from Russian: "I already have a solution for collecting analytics from all sites (the xronocode dashboard) ... let it further collect, it just needs to also learn to collect downloads and updates data"). (2) The dashboard's intake is the natural carrier: it is server-to-server by design (src/api/app.ts: "Server-to-server only: the key never reaches a browser"), accepts per-site ingest keys with an optional origin bound (none for server keys), validates events with a lower-case dotted name, a required session key, optional props (verified in src/core/collect.ts validateEvent, 2026-11-03), and deduplicates by (site_key, idempotency_key) so retries are safe. (3) What the owner sees stays what he already knows: he logs into his dashboard (Google OAuth) and the update numbers appear next to his sites' data; nothing new is asked of him beyond one ingest key issued by his own dashboard.

Goals.R-1: Push, do not pull: on every valid counted event the gateway additionally sends one event to https://dash.xronocode.com/api/v1/collect — mark.update_check with props {os, from} for /feed, mark.update_pkg with props {platform, version} for /pkg. Body shape {events:[{id, name, ts, session:"gateway", props}]} with id from crypto.randomUUID(), ts integer ms at send time; authenticated by the x-collect-key header with env.DASH_COLLECT_KEY. The push rides ctx.waitUntil next to the Analytics Engine write: best-effort, response-changing never — failures and non-2XX answers are swallowed, nothing is logged, no retry, no queue, at most one dashboard subrequest per counting request (the AE write plus the push stay far inside the 50-subrequest free limit).
Goals.R-2: Off by absence: an unset or empty DASH_COLLECT_KEY secret disables the push completely — zero dashboard fetches, counting behaves exactly as before. This is the deploy-time switch: the code can ship before the owner issues the key, and the key turns the flow on the moment it is set (no redeploy needed).
Goals.R-3: Counting semantics unchanged where it matters: /feed and /pkg keep their validation, derived-only Locations, GET-only gate and plain-404 classes byte-identical in behavior; the Analytics Engine datapoint write is untouched (the dashboard push is an additional sink, not a replacement); /stats and its secrets are untouched by this change (the route stays dormant 502 until some future decision retires or revives it). The privacy posture is unchanged in kind: the dashboard receives the same aggregate dimensions the Analytics Engine already stores (event kind, OS/platform, version), no IP, no user agent relay (the worker sends none), no identifiers; the receiver is the owner's own system.
Goals.R-4: Secrets hygiene: the only new secret name is DASH_COLLECT_KEY; no token or key value in the repository (the existing secrets scan pins extend naturally — the shape bans already cover ingest keys, which are 40-plus-character tokens); the dead STATS_API_TOKEN secret (unusable value from the failed provisioning) is deleted from the worker, and the dead Cloudflare token mark-stats-reader is deleted from the account — both are cleanup, executed owner-side via the dashboard.
Goals.R-5: README truth: the gateway README's privacy and data-flow sentences are amended to disclose the dashboard push (aggregate event dimensions, owner's own dashboard, best-effort) and to document the one setup step — issue a site ingest key named for the mark gateway in the dashboard, set it as the worker secret DASH_COLLECT_KEY; no Cloudflare API token is documented anywhere anymore (the Readout access section's STATS_API_TOKEN instructions are removed as part of R-4's cleanup story, the section trimmed to what remains true).
Goals.R-6: Governance: M-071's MODULE_CONTRACT PURPOSE/SCOPE grows "events are additionally pushed best-effort to the owner's analytics dashboard (C-STATS-DASH-PUSH)", MODULE_MAP grows the push locals, VERSION and CHANGE_SUMMARY bump; V-M-071 gains the push pins (event shape, key header, off-by-absence, swallow-on-failure, response-unchanged). This change supersedes the C-UPDATER-STATS R-7 freeze for the counting handlers in the minimal sense of the added waitUntil push; every other frozen property stands.

Constraints.Item: Owner basis (2026-11-03, translated): "the dashboard already collects everything fine, let it further collect — it just needs to also learn to collect downloads and updates data" plus the order "го" — this change is the gateway half of that order (the dashboard half — a GitHub downloads collector and a display section — lives in the dashboard's own repository under its own rules).

Best-effort or nothing: a dashboard outage, a rejected batch, or an absent key must never change any counting response — the redirect always returns exactly as today; the push adds no logs and no new error bodies.

No new data: the pushed event carries only dimensions the gateway already counts (event kind, OS/platform, version); session is the fixed string "gateway"; no request-derived metadata (no IP, no UA relay, no geo) is sent.

Contract fidelity: the event must satisfy the dashboard's validator exactly (lower-case dotted name, id 1-64 of A-Za-z0-9_-, session 1-64, integer-ms ts at send time, props of short string values) — verified against src/core/collect.ts of the dashboard repository on 2026-11-03; deviations mean the batch is dropped silently, so the shape is pinned by unit tests.
No Cloudflare API tokens: none created, stored or documented by this change; the only credential is the dashboard's own site ingest key (owner-issued in his dashboard UI, one secret).
Existing gates stay green: the gateway suite (48 tests) with the new push pins, npm test, grace lint current/target/final against the recorded baseline.

NonGoals.NonGoal: The dashboard half — a GitHub downloads collector and the display section — lives in the dashboard repository (avenex-outreach/analytics-dashboard) under its own AGENTS.md; this change touches only the mark repository.
Any read path from Cloudflare Analytics Engine: no STATS_API_TOKEN, no SQL API calls, no revival of the /stats readout (the route stays as-is, dormant).
Batching, queuing, retries or aggregation windows — one event per counted request, fire-and-forget; the dashboard's (site_key, id) dedup already makes retries unnecessary.
Any new dimension on the counted events; any change to what /feed and /pkg validate or where they redirect.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Push behavior: a valid /feed request produces exactly one dashboard POST with body {events:[{id, name:"mark.update_check", ts (integer ms, ~now), session:"gateway", props:{os, from}}]} and header x-collect-key equal to the test fixture key; a valid /pkg request likewise with name "mark.update_pkg" and props {platform, version}; the 302 responses are byte-identical with and without the push.
Off by absence: with DASH_COLLECT_KEY unset or empty, zero dashboard fetches occur (pinned with a fetch-counting stub); the Analytics Engine write still happens.

Swallow-on-failure: a dashboard non-2XX or network rejection changes nothing — the redirect returns, no error body, no log line, no retry (pinned); the counting suite's existing 48 tests stay green without expectation changes.

Secrets hygiene: the secrets-name-only scan over the touched files stays clean (only DASH_COLLECT_KEY joins the allowed names); the README documents the one-key setup and no longer documents any Cloudflare API token; the worker's STATS_API_TOKEN secret and the account's mark-stats-reader token are deleted (dashboard-side cleanup, recorded as owner-side evidence).

Governance: M-071 contract/map amended with VERSION and CHANGE_SUMMARY bumps; V-M-071 carries the push pins; npx vitest run tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs, npm test and grace lint for this change are green against the recorded baseline; the implementation review gate closes with two consecutive clean four-corner passes before the PR is proposed.

AffectedAreas.Item: tools/stats-gateway/worker.mjs — the pushDash helper (module-scope constant URL, waitUntil fetch, swallow-all), called from handleFeed and handlePkg after the existing count() call; contract header amendments.

tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs — push pins: event shape and key header per route, off-by-absence (zero fetches), swallow-on-failure, response byte-equality; the secrets scan's allowed-names list gains DASH_COLLECT_KEY.
tools/stats-gateway/README.md — the dashboard-push disclosure and the one-key setup step; the STATS_API_TOKEN instructions removed.
.grace/graph/features.xml and .grace/verification/features.xml — M-071/V-M-071 amendments routed in the same bundle as the code.
Explicitly untouched: tables.mjs, query.mjs (all modes), wrangler.toml, /stats route and its secrets, src/**, src-tauri/**, .github/**.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npx vitest run tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs && npm test && grace lint --path . --change C-STATS-DASH-PUSH --assertions final --run-commands (live push behavior is owner-verified after the key is set: dashboard shows mark.update_check events within minutes)
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Unit pins for the four acceptance behaviors; the existing 48 pins unchanged; lint clean against the baseline; post-deploy owner-side evidence: the dashboard's mark site shows the first events.

Assumptions.Assumption: Dashboard contract facts verified 2026-11-03 against the dashboard repository (avenex-outreach/analytics-dashboard): POST /api/v1/collect with x-collect-key (or ?key=), keys are sha256-hashed server-side, the origin check applies only when the key has an originHost bound (server keys: none), validateEvent requires a lower-case dotted name (max 64), an id of 1-64 [A-Za-z0-9_-], a session of the same alphabet, optional props; insert dedups by (site_key, id). The owner issues site ingest keys in his dashboard UI ("Выдать ключ", value shown once) — a flow he already uses for three sites.

The owner's order "го" (2026-11-03) approves this spec and its lean plan; the gate budget concentrates on the implementation review (two consecutive clean four-corner passes), matching the execution-wave pattern.
